stories.head: Linnworks CMO exposes hidden manual work inside 'automated' marketing operations
stories.plain: Hilary Smith of Linnworks argues that most so-called automated marketing pipelines still rely on hidden manual labour to function. For teams evaluating AI-driven stacks, this is a useful reality check: automation claims often overstate true coverage, meaning governance and operational audits matter before buying or building further.

stories.head: Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.7 billion, reshaping the customer engagement platform market
stories.plain: Salesforce's $5.7 billion acquisition of Braze is one of the biggest martech deals in years. It brings a leading customer engagement platform directly into the Salesforce ecosystem, changing the competitive landscape for every vendor selling messaging, journey orchestration, or real-time engagement tools — and forcing buyers to reconsider their stack.

stories.head: EngageLab launches Agent Email: AI agents that receive, understand, and reply to customer emails at scale
stories.plain: EngageLab's Agent Email lets AI agents handle inbound customer replies — not just outbound sends — grounding answers in a private knowledge base and writing intent signals back to CRM. This is a meaningful shift: AI moves from composing messages to autonomously managing two-way conversations, changing how email is bought and governed.

stories.head: Limelit launches agentic GEO platform with MCP server giving AI assistants 211 tools to automate AI-search visibility
stories.plain: Limelit connects Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor directly to a GEO workflow engine via an MCP server, letting AI agents track brand visibility across six AI search engines and autonomously create approved content to close gaps. It is the first platform purpose-built to automate the entire generative engine optimization loop, not just report on it.

stories.head: Peec AI launches Peec Agent to let marketing teams act on what AI search engines say about their brand
stories.plain: Used by 3,500+ companies, Peec AI now adds an autonomous agent layer that converts AI search audit findings into prioritised technical, content, and third-party actions. This matters because it closes the loop between monitoring AI-answer visibility and actually improving it — a capability marketers will increasingly need to buy or build.

stories.head: ChatGPT sends less than 1% of Google's traffic — but converts at a higher rate
stories.plain: New data shows Google organic still drives 27× more conversions than all LLMs combined, yet ChatGPT visitors convert at a higher rate when they do arrive. This benchmark is essential for any marketer deciding how much budget to shift toward GEO versus traditional SEO — and it puts real numbers on a heavily hyped debate.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Taking the Wheel Across the Full Marketing Stack
body: The past 30 days produced a flood of product launches where AI moved from assistant to autonomous operator: agents that receive and reply to customer emails, agents that build and edit websites via MCP servers, and multi-agent platforms that coordinate specialised bots the way a team of humans would. This is no longer a chatbot upgrade — it is a structural shift in who (or what) executes marketing workflows.

The bottleneck is now data reliability, not capability. MarTech's guide to building a source of truth for AI agents signals that teams investing in agent infrastructure must first solve the unglamorous problem of clean, authoritative inputs — or risk automating at scale on a shaky foundation.
ev: MarTech · Source of Truth for Agents

themes.head: GEO Replaces SEO as the Visibility Battleground
body: AI search engines are converting user prompts into structured research sessions, bypassing traditional blue-link results and the traffic they once delivered. The data point that crystallises the shift: ChatGPT sends less than 1% of Google's referral traffic — yet AI-generated answers are already shaping what products consumers consider, making presence in those answers commercially critical.

A new category of tooling — Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) — is emerging to meet this need. Limelit's launch of 211 autonomous-agent tools and Peec AI's brand-monitoring agent are early signs that managing how AI systems represent your brand will become as routine as managing paid search bids.
ev: MarTech · AI Search as Customer Research

themes.head: Composable, Modular Architecture Becomes the Default Expectation
body: Monolithic martech suites are losing ground to composable stacks where best-in-class components snap together via open APIs and standards like MCP. Framer's launch of an official MCP server — letting any external AI agent build and edit websites — and GeeLark's expansion of cloud-phone workflows via API, CLI, & MCP are concrete signals that interoperability is now a product requirement, not a roadmap item.

For decision-makers, this means vendor selection criteria must shift: the question is no longer 'does this platform do everything?' but 'how easily does it connect to everything else?' Teams that build on composable principles now will avoid expensive re-platforming cycles as AI capabilities evolve rapidly.

themes.head: Personalisation Pivots from Identity to Intent
body: A quiet but consequential reframe is underway: effective personalisation is shifting from knowing who someone is (identity, demographics, cookies) to knowing what they want right now (intent signals, behavioural context, decision moments). This matters because identity-based targeting is eroding under privacy regulation, while intent signals remain accessible and actionable.

This connects directly to the 'journeys to decisions' framing gaining traction in customer-engagement strategy. Rather than mapping a linear path, marketers are being urged to intercept the micro-decisions that actually determine purchase — a model that rewards real-time signal processing over static segmentation.

themes.head: The Hidden Manual Layer Undermines Automation ROI
body: Across operations, e-commerce, and marketing, a recurring finding is that tools marketed as automated still depend on significant invisible human labour — spreadsheet fixes, exception handling, data wrangling — that never shows up in the vendor demo. Linnworks's Hilary Smith puts a name to it: the manual work embedded inside supposedly automated operations is both a cost and a risk that leaders routinely undercount.

The implication for AI investment decisions is sharp: before adding another AI layer, organisations need an honest audit of where humans are currently patching broken processes. Skipping that audit means AI acceleration will amplify existing fragility rather than eliminate it — a lesson underscored by the parallel finding that adding AI or headcount alone cannot close a marketing skills gap.
ev: MarTech · AI Won't Fix a Skills Gap

month.takeaway: The month's signal is unified: AI is graduating from tool to autonomous operator across every marketing function, and the organisations that will benefit are those that fix their data foundations, embrace composable architecture, and audit the manual labour hiding inside their 'automated' stacks before they scale.
